source: KICD Creative Activities, First Published in 2021; Revised in 2024 (text layer)
status: outcomes from KICD's text, word for word; skills, prerequisites and misconceptions not yet mapped

content_topics: Jump for height and distance (forward, backward, right and left),
learning_experiences: watch a video clip or a demonstration on jumping activities,
practise different ways of jumping with peers,
identify and collect locally available materials for improvising objects to be used in jumping while observing safety,
jump high for height and far in different directions,
collaboratively sing songs while jumping high and far in different ways,
talk about their own and others' performance in jumping activities.
key_inquiry_questions: Why are jumping activities important as a physical activity?
Which objects can be improvised for use in jumping activities?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Creativity and Imagination: the learner improvises and creatively makes objects for jumping using locally available materials.
Communication and Collaboration: the learner talks about different ways of jumping with peers,
sub_strands.values:
Responsibility: the learner observes safety precautions when collecting appropriate materials for making uprights.
Unity: the learner cooperates with others while singing appropriate action songs as they jump high and far.
sub_strands.pcis:
Safety: the learner observes safety while collecting appropriate materials for making uprights to be used in jumping.
Self-awareness: the learner becomes aware of their ability to jumping high and far in different directions.
sub_strands.links: Mathematics Activities: the learner counts while jumping high and far.

outcomes.text: identify different ways of jumping for body agility
improvise objects to be used for jumping
jump in different ways for coordination
sing songs while jumping for fun
appreciate jumping for enjoyment while observing safety

learning_experiences: identify and imitate objects that maintain a constant beat such as a ticking clock,
collaboratively tap/clap the beat using body percussion; clapping/tapping/marching/stamping the foot while singing simple songs,
watch live or recorded performances to identify body percussion accompaniments to songs,
explore their body and use body percussions to accompany familiar topical songs,
improvise body percussion accompaniments to songs,
record performances using a digital device or present to peers for feedback.
key_inquiry_questions: Why is it importrant to maintain a steady in music?
How can body percussions be used to create a rhythm?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Self-efficacy: the learner confidently accompanies songs using body percussion rhythmic accompaniment with peers.
Learning to learn: the learner identifies and keenly taps/claps the beat of a song.
sub_strands.values:
Unity: the learner cooperates with others when performing rhythmic accomapnhiment using body percussions.
Love: the learner provides constructive feedback to peers’ performances.
sub_strands.pcis: Environment conservation: the learner sings and accompanies topical songs on issues such as Environmental conservation.
sub_strands.links:
Environmental Activities: the learner internalises words of songs on Environmental issues.
English Language activities: the learner communicates through words of songs.

outcomes.text: identify items that maintain a steady pulse for beat articulation
play a steady beat on a percussion instrument while singing
create a rhythmic accompaniment to a song using body percussion
appreciate the use of percussions in creating rhythm

content_topics: Lines; straight, wavy, zigzag and curved lines Direction; vertical, diagonal and horizontal,
learning_experiences: observe actual and virtual pictures and identify lines,
collaboratively, recognise straight, wavy, curved and zigzag lines within the environment,
select appropriate materials for drawing such as coloured pencils, crayons, and charcoal among others,
draw various lines; straight, wavy, curved and zigzag,
draw the lines in different directions; vertical, diagonal and horizontal,
create a pattern by drawing lines in different directions,
draw simple pictures using lines for enjoyment,
show and speak clearly about own and others’ drawing for feedback.
key_inquiry_questions: What tools are used in drawing?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Creativity and Imagination: the learner draws lines in different direction; vertical, diagonal and horizontal.
Communication and collaboration: the learner speaks clearly about own and others’ drawing for feedback.
sub_strands.values:
Unity: the learner collaboratively, recognise straight, wavy, curved and zigzag lines within the environment
Responsibility: the learner cares for resources as they source appropriate materials for drawing such as coloured pencils, crayons, charcoal
sub_strands.pcis: Health promotion: the learner observes hygiene by properly washing hands after using found objects in the environment to draw.
sub_strands.links:
Mathematical Activities: the learner applies the line drawing skills acquired in Mathematics to draw various lines in the environment.
Environmental Activities: the learner names various lines in their environment.

outcomes.text: identify lines for familiarity
draw lines in different directions
draw patterns using lines in different directions
appreciate drawing pictures for expression

content_topics: Stretching positions (standing, sitting, kneeling and lying).
learning_experiences: talk about body parts involved in stretching,
demonstrate stretching in different directions with peers,
practise stretching in different directions,
practise stretching in different positions,
collaboratively, play appropriate games involving stretching while observing safety,
sing action songs on body parts involved in stretching,
team up to use digital devices to record performances on stretching for future reference.
key_inquiry_questions: Why is stretching important as a physical activity?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Communication and Collaboration: the learner actively talks about parts of the body that are used in stretching.
Creativity and Imagination: the learner creatively stretches in directions and in positions.
Digital literacy: the learner uses digital devices to record performances on stretching.
sub_strands.values:
Responsibility: the learner observes safety of self and others during stretching activities.
Love: the learner appreciates the ability of others stretching in different positions.
sub_strands.pcis: Safety and security: the learner stretches to a reasonable limit to avoid injuries while in different positions.
sub_strands.links: Environmental Activities: the learner stretches to different directions of the compass point.

outcomes.text: identify body parts involved in stretching
perform stretching in different directions for flexibility
enjoy stretching in different directions for body fitness

learning_experiences: observe actual and virtual environment to; identify materials and tools for painting and colouring,
apply colour within the pictures using dry media to represent colours of objects in the environment,
paint using a brush within the shapes of the picture on paper,
paint using fingers on a paper or fabric,
use sponge to paint within drawn forms on a paper or fabric, take note; clean hands after painting,
display the pictures and talk about them with your peers.
key_inquiry_questions: Which tools can be used in painting?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Critical Thinking and Problem Solving: the learner identifies materials and tools for painting and experiments with different techniques like using fingers and sponges.
Creativity and Imagination: the learner colours pictures and experiments painting using fingers, brushes and sponge for enjoyment.
Self-efficacy: the learner gains confidence as they engage in painting using different tools and display their pictures.
sub_strands.values:
Unity: the learner promotes a sense of unity as they engage in painting activities with peers, collaboratively shares ideas, and appreciate each other's artwork.
Responsibility: the learner takes responsibility for their artistic choices and creations, recognizing the impact of their actions on the final artwork.
sub_strands.pcis: Safety and hygiene: as the learner clean their hands after painting using fingers, sponge and a brush on the paper or fabric.
sub_strands.links: Mathematics Activities: the learner applies the skill of counting to mix paint and paint using a brush within the shapes of the picture on paper.

outcomes.text: identify materials and tools for painting and colouring
colour a picture to immitate the environment
paint shapes using a brush
paint using fingers on a surface
paint using a sponge on a surface
enjoy painting and colouring as a form of expression

learning_experiences: collaboratively listen to a variety of sounds and identify them as melodic or non-melodic,
listen to songs and aurally identify the passages as like or unlike,
listen to age-appropriate live or recorded melodic patterns and imitate through singing or humming with pitch accuracy.
comment on peers’ imitation of melodies using polite language.
key_inquiry_questions: Why are melodic sounds important?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Self-efficacy: the learner gains confidence as they imitate a melody by singing or humming.
Communication and collaboration: the learner keenly listens to a melody and clearly echoes it.
sub_strands.values:
Unity: the learner cooperates with others to listen and distinguish sounds as melodic and non-melodic.
Social justice: the learner shares own opinion and gives peers a chance to express their opinion on sounds.
sub_strands.pcis: Self-esteem: the learner gains confidence while echoing melodies played.
sub_strands.links: English/Kiswahili language activities: the learner listens keenly and speaks clearly about the sounds they listen to.

outcomes.text: identify sounds as melodic or non-melodic for aural discrimination
aurally recognise like and unlike passages in short melodies
echo simple melodic patterns by singing or humming for aural skill development
enjoy replicating melodic passages for aural discrimination

learning_experiences: explore virtual and actual source to identify letter and numeral patterns,
use letters to create a line pattern,
use numerals to create a line pattern,
take turns to show and talk about patterns created by self and others.
key_inquiry_questions: How is a pattern made?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Creativity and Imagination: the learner explores various numerals and letters to create line patterns.
Learning to Learn: the learner explores virtual and actual source to identify letter and numeral patterns.
sub_strands.values: Respect: the learner take turns to show and talk about patterns created by self and others.
sub_strands.pcis: Cultural Heritage: the learner creates patterns inspired by cultural elements within their surrounding.
sub_strands.links: Mathematical Activities: the learner applies mathematical concepts in pattern-making involves such as sequencing and repetition, providing a cross-disciplinary connection to mathematical activities.

outcomes.text: recognise patterns made using numeral and letters
create patterns using letters
make a pattern using numerals
enjoy making patterns for expression

content_topics: Performance aspects; songs, game activities, pattern formations, the use of props, observance of safety and appropriate etiquette (behaviour).
learning_experiences: watch live or recorded performances of singing games drawn from Kenyan local cultures and talk about them,
identify props used in a singing game performance by name,
collect relevant locally available materials and improvise a prop for use in singing games, performance observing safety,

take a role and perform age-appropriate singing games with peers focussing on performance aspects; singing, game activities, pattern formations, the use of props, observance of safety and appropriate etiquette (behaviour).
key_inquiry_questions: Why are singing games performed?
Why are props used in a singing game?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Self-efficacy: the learner confidently makes a variety of body movements while performing singing games.
Learning to learn: the learner learns to perform singing games from various Kenyan cultures.
Citizenship: the learner takes pride in performing singing games drawn from diverse Kenyan communities.
sub_strands.values:
Responsibility: the learner takes up a role in the performance of a singing game from a Kenyan community.
Unity: the learner works with others to perform a singing game from a Kenyan culture.
sub_strands.pcis:
Personal hygiene: the learner collects appropriate locally available materials for making simple paper costumes.
Self-awareness and self-esteem: the learner makes a variety of movements that are appropriate while performing the singing game which boosts their morale.
sub_strands.links: Indigenous Language Activities: the learner sings varied songs in indigenous languages.

outcomes.text: identify props used in the performance of a singing game from a Kenyan community
improvise a simple prop for use in performing a singing game
perform singing games drawn from local cultures in Kenyan for enjoyment
enjoy performing singing games from Kenyan local cultures

learning_experiences: collect locally available reusable materials to be used for making a ball while observing hygiene,
make an appropriate ball using collected materials,
practise throwing and catching activities using the ball with peers while observing safety,
play simple games on throwing and catching a ball,
talk about own and others effort while playing games involving throwing and catching.
key_inquiry_questions: Which direction is easier to throw and catch the ball from during play?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Self-efficacy: the learner confidently throws and catches the ball while playing with peers.
Learning to learn: the learner keenly follows the steps of knotting when making a ball.
sub_strands.values:
Unity: the learner cooperates with others when throwing and catching a ball.
Love: the learner shares materials while making a ball.
sub_strands.pcis: Environment Conservation: the learner uses reusable locally available materials to improvise a ball.
sub_strands.links:
Environmental activities: the learner observes hygiene while using reusable locally available materials to improvise a ball.
English activities: the learner communicates with peers while throwing and catching a ball.

outcomes.text: identify materials used to improvise a ball
improvise a ball from locally available materials
perform throwing and catching activities for skill acquisition
appreciate throwing and catching activities for enjoyment

learning_experiences: observe virtual or actual pictures of items made out of paper,
collect varied recyclable papers for craft,
create paper toys using the pleating technique such as animals, fan among others,
use the folding technique to make toy items to imitate things in the environment,
narrate to peers about and/or play with the paper item.
key_inquiry_questions: Which items can you make using paper?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Communication and Collaboration: the learner engages in showcasing, discussing, and playing with their own and others' paper craft creations.
Creativity and Imagination: the learner makes paper items that allows them to explore through transforming paper into playful items.
Learning to Learn: the learner acquires paper crafting skills and techniques.
sub_strands.values:
Love: the learner derives joy from making and playing with peers.
Unity: the learner narrates to peers about and/ or play with the paper item.
sub_strands.pcis: Life skills: the learner develops self-awareness and self-esteem through narrating about their work to express their feelings, ideas and emotions.
sub_strands.links:
Mathematical Activities: the learner applies mathematical concepts in pleating and folding.
Environmental Activities: the learner collect varied recyclable papers for craft in the environment.

outcomes.text: identify items made using paper craft
make paper items using the pleating technique
make paper items using the folding technique
play using the paper items for enjoyment

learning_experiences: watch a video clip or a demonstration of a log roll,
watch a video clip or demonstration of a T-balance,
collect and share reusable materials for making markers to be used during the log roll and T-balance performance with peers,
work collaboratively to make markers and mark the open space using improvised markers,
perform the log roll in different directions while observing safety,
perform the T-balance in different with peers while observing safety,
sing action songs while performing log roll and T-balance,
talk about own and others performance of the log roll and T - balance.
key_inquiry_questions: Why should there be good spacing while performing the log roll and T-balance?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Creativity and imagination: the learner identifies simple reusable materials, and makes markers.
Communication and Collaboration: the learner talks about others performance of the log roll and T-balance,
sub_strands.values:
Love: the learner shares simple reusable materials with peers.
Respect: the learner portrays positive regard for self and others as they work in groups.
sub_strands.pcis:
Health promotion issues: the learner observes safety when collecting materials to be used in making markers.
Environmental conservation: the learner collects reusable materials.
sub_strands.links:
Environmental activities: the learner observes hygiene while collecting and sharing simple reusable materials.
Religious Activities: the learner applies values while positively talking about others' performance.

outcomes.text: identify log roll and T-balance through practice
make markers for use during log rolls and T-balance performance
perform a log roll for coordination
perform the T-balance for flexibility
appreciate performing the log roll and T-balance for enjoyment

content_topics: Performance techniques; - accuracy of tune and rhythm,
learning_experiences: watch live or recorded performances of age-appropriate action songs and imitate the performances,
collaboratively listen to or perform action songs based on pertinent issues and talk about the message in the action songs,
sing action songs in unison focusing on performance techniques;
respectfully talk about peers’ performances for improvement.
key_inquiry_questions: Why do we sing with actions?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Communication and Collaboration: the learner exhibits teamwork as they discuss with peers the message of action songs.
Creativity and imagination: the learner utilises appropriate actions in the performance of an action song.
sub_strands.values:
Respect: the learner critiques peers’ performances of action songs using polite language.
Unity: the learner collaborates with peers to talk about and perform action songs.
sub_strands.pcis:
Self-esteem: the learner gains confidence through performance of an action song individually.
Health Education: the learner discusses and performs action songs on health-related issues.
sub_strands.links: English/Kiswahili Language activities: the learner utilises listening and speaking skills to discuss the messages of action songs.

outcomes.text: describe the message in an action song
sing action songs in unison applying performance techniques
enjoy singing action songs for self-expression

learning_experiences: observe actual or virtual items modelled using the pinch method,
collect materials and tools for use in the pinch method modelling.
model simple objects using the pinch method,
showcase, talk about own and others’ work.
key_inquiry_questions: What items in the are modelled using the pinch method?
What materials and tools are used for modelling?
What items would you like to model?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Critical Thinking and Problem-Solving: the learner identifies materials and tools for modelling through observation of actual or virtual items, showcasing critical thinking skills in selecting appropriate resources for the pinch method.
Creativity and Imagination: the learner utilises the pinch method, to model simple objects, demonstrating creativity and imagination in transforming materials into unique and expressive creations.
Learning to Learn: the learner collects materials and tools for pinch method modelling, they develop skills in adaptability and continuous improvement, embodying the concept of learning to learn in the artistic process.
Self-Efficacy: the learner builds confidence as they actively participate in modelling using the pinch method.
sub_strands.values:
Love: the learner to expresses emotions and ideas, as they showcase, talk about own and others' work.
Unity: the learner engages in discussions about modelled items and share ideas as they appreciate each other's artistic creations.
Responsibility: the learner takes responsibility for their artistic choices and creations, recognizing the impact of their actions on the final modelled items.
Patriotism: the learner explores themes related to the local culture through modelling to foster a sense of patriotism and pride in national identity.
sub_strands.pcis:
Cultural Expression: the learner models items that can be linked to cultural expressions, local traditions and heritage.
Sustainability: the learner considers environmentally friendly materials for modelling that addresses contemporary concerns about sustainability, promoting responsible artistic practises.
sub_strands.links:
Environmental Activities: the learner models and creates objects that represent elements of the environment while improvising and using found materials.
Mathematical Activities: the learner applies the process of modelling involves measurement and proportion, integrating mathematical concepts into artistic activities.

outcomes.text: identify items modelled using the pinch method
identify materials and tools used in modelling
model items using the pinch method
enjoy modelling items using the pinch method

content_topics: Percussion musical instruments: Shakers, jingles and drums.
Methods of playing a shaker-shaking, hitting and scrapping
learning_experiences: search for percussion instruments from print and electronic media and identify them by name,
responsibly collect appropriate available materials and improvise a shaker or jingle,
display and positively talk about percussion instruments improvised by peers and self and store them for future use,
visit actual or virtual sites to watch or observe how percussion instruments are played,
practice the methods of playing shakers, jingles and drums,
play a percussion musical instrument to accompany singing.
key_inquiry_questions: Why are percussion musical instruments played?
How can percussion instruments be improvised?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Communication and Collaboration: the learner exhibits teamwork as they play drums, jingles and shakers to accompany singing in a group.
Creativity and imagination: the learner undertakes tasks that require skills to improvise shakers and jingles using locally available materials.
Digital literacy: the learner searches for and identifies percussion instruments from digital sites.
Citizenship: the learner interacts with real or virtual percussion instruments drawn from different Kenyan communities.
sub_strands.values:
Responsibility: the learner clears the working areas after improvising shakers and jingles using locally available materials and stores them.
Unity: the learner works harmoniously with peers while naming and improvising percussion instruments..
sub_strands.pcis:
Environmental conservation: the learner responsibly uses locally available materials to improvise percussion instruments.
Patriotism: the learner identifies, improvises and plays instruments from Kenyan communities for cultural expression.
sub_strands.links: Indigenous language activities: the learner identifies percussion musical instruments from different Kenyan communities by their indigenous names.

outcomes.text: identify percussion musical instruments from diverse indigenous Kenyan communities
improvise a percussion musical instrument using locally available materials
play a percussion musical instrument for enjoyment
appreciate percussion musical instruments from diverse Kenyan cultural communities

content_topics: Sources of sound-Birds, animals, humans and objects
Elements of music: − Volume-Loud or soft sound, − Speed-Fast/slow sound − Pitch-High or low sound,
learning_experiences: keenly listen to sounds (birds, humans, animals, objects) within the school environment and identify their sources,
identify high and low sounds from the environment,
collaboratively listen to live/recorded music and describe its volume, speed and pitch, using appropriate terminology such as; loud/soft, fast/slow and high/ low,
listen to and respond imaginatively to sounds in the environment through; movement, imitation or talking about it,
talk about the mood of selected pieces of short music either as happy or sad.
key_inquiry_questions: 1 Why is it important to listen to music?
How does listening to music make you feel?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Communication and Collaboration: the learner listens keenly to songs and clearly talks about it using appropriate terminology.
Creativity and Imagination: the learner responds to music imaginatively.
sub_strands.values:
Unity: the learner works with peers to discuss music listened to.
Respect: the learner appreciates peers’ imitations of the identified sounds of birds, animals and objects.
sub_strands.pcis: Safety and security: the learner observes their own and others' safety as they walk around the school environment identifying various sounds of birds, animals and objects.
sub_strands.links:
English, Kiswahili and Indigenous Languages Activities: the learner uses language skills learnt to express self when imitating the identified sounds of birds, animals and objects.
Environmental Activities: the learner applies knowledge gained in Environmental Activities to role play, imitate and identify sounds of various birds, animals and objects.

outcomes.text: identify sounds in the local environment for aural discrimination
describe the elements of music as used in a song
respond to sounds in the environment for self-expression
describe the mood of songs for emotional expression
enjoy listening to and talking about music

learning_experiences: observe pictures of different water points at home and share with peers,
talk about water points at home,
talk about the dangers of water points at home with peers,
collect pictures of familiar water points from magazines, newspapers among others,
sort and cut out the pictures,
stick using glue side by side the pictures on a stiff paper to make a simple montage,
perform a singing game about the dangers of water,
show the montage work and talk about ways to be safe around water points at homes,
observe safety measures around water points at home by exercising self-discipline.
key_inquiry_questions: How can water points at home be dangerous?
What materials are used to make a montage?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Communication and collaboration: the learner talks about the dangers of water points at home with peers.
Learning to learn: the learner learns to observe safety measures around different water points at home.
sub_strands.values:
Responsibility: the learner observes safety precautions around water points at home.
Integrity: the learner exercises self-discipline around water points at home.
sub_strands.pcis:
Health promotion: the learner practises self-discipline around water points at home to avoid injuries
Safety: the learner develops water safety awareness by practising safety measures around water points at home
sub_strands.links:
Environmental Activities: the learner practises water safety awareness within at home.
Religious Activities: the learner applies values of self-discipline around water points at home.

outcomes.text: recognise different water points around the home environment
identify water dangers arising from water points at home
make a montage of water points around the home environment
narrate ways of applying safety around water points at home
appreciate water safety at home for life skills

indicators.indicator: Ability to create or execute: − a steady beat on a percussion instrument − rhythmic accompaniment to a song using body percussions − objects to be used for jumping, − jump in different ways, − songs while jumping for fun, − draw different lines − stretch in different directions − colour a picture − paint shapes − like and unlike passages in a melody − echo a simple melody − patterns using letters − patterns using numerals.

levels.EE: Creates and executes the 13 skills of Creative Activities skilfully.
levels.ME: Creates and executes all the 13 skills of Creative Activities accurately.
levels.AE: Creates and executes 12 to 8 skills of Creative Activities.
levels.BE: Creates and executes 7 or less skills of Creative Activities.

indicators.indicator: Ability to perform and/or display - singing game African style, - use props - throwing and catching activities - make paper items using pleating - make paper items using folding techniques - log roll - an action song - T- balance - percussion musical instrument - model items using the pinch method

levels.EE: Performs and/or displays the 11 items of Creative activities skillfully and/or creatively.
levels.ME: Performs and/or displays the 11 items of Creative activities
levels.AE: Performs and/or displays the 10-6 items in Creative Activities.
levels.BE: Performs and/or displays 5 or less items of Creative Activities.

indicators.indicator: Ability to appreciate and/ or analyse: - sources of sounds - elements of music (volume, speed, pitch) -mood of music -water dangers -safety around water points -water points around home

levels.EE: Appreciates and/or analyses the 6 Creative activities items in detail.
levels.ME: Appreciates and/or analyses the 6 Creative activities items.
levels.AE: Appreciates and/or analyses the 5-3 items in Creative activities.
levels.BE: Appreciates and/or analyses the 3 or less Creative activities items.
